title: Minimax Average Treatment Effect Rates under Dyadic-Shell Overlap Decay
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 (typed) BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR — D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field (target=field).
gap_reasons: Delivered tier subfield < floor field; directed reroute: Replace the two-reservoir lower-bound witness with a construction valid without the lower- and upper-shell-richness inequalities, and extend both the risk converse and honest-length converse to the broader class already covered by the estimator.

The matched equivalences are proved only after imposing the lower- and upper-shell-richness inequalities, numerical restrictions tailored to the bespoke two-reservoir lower-bound witness; on the broader uniform one-sided-shell class, the note proves only upper bounds and coverage.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived and fully reviewed the corrected four-channel minimax and honest-length frontier for the oracle public-function ATE experiment, including explicit shell-preserving least-favourable families, the critical logarithmic case, an all-N finite-threshold estimator bound, and computable interval calibration. Math and decision-panel reviews passed with zero findings, but the final general referee graded the result subfield because matching converses require reservoir-rich shell constants whereas only upper bounds extend to the broader uniform-shell class. A future field-tier re-raise must construct matching risk and honest-length converses for every feasible shell-constant geometry (or establish a valid inclusion bridge), rather than re-derive the completed restricted-class theorem.
tldr: For fixed one-sided dyadic-shell constants satisfying both \(\texttt{ass:lower-shell-richness}\) and \(\texttt{ass:upper-shell-richness}\), the absolute-risk, root-MSE, fixed-probability for each fixed \(\delta\in(0,\delta_0]\), and honest expected-length for each fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/4)\) frontiers all equal the four-channel rate \(\rho_n\) up to constants.  The clipped estimator, five-block median, and interval upper bounds hold on the broader uniform one-sided-shell class with those two richness conditions deleted.  An exported all-\(N\) inequality gives \(E_P|\widehat\tau_{\lambda,N}-\tau(P)|\leq C_{\mathrm{FT}}U_N(\lambda)\), the explicit oracle comparison gives \(U_n(\lambda_n^\star)\leq C_{\mathrm{opt}}\rho_n\), and \(C_\star=C_{\mathrm{FT}}C_{\mathrm{opt}}\) yields the computable interval multiplier \(K_\alpha=C_\star\max\{\sqrt{10}(10/\alpha)^{1/3},\alpha^{-1}\}\).  Adaptation to unknown shell and nuisance certificates remains open.
gap: Regular-overlap structure-agnostic theory gives a nuisance-product benchmark, while weak-overlap papers give trimming rules, irregular limits, or sufficient Wald conditions. MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026DRWeakOverlap, Theorem 3.1 and Proposition B.1, is especially close on target preservation: its bias-corrected trimmed doubly robust method retains the original ATE and yields asymptotic inference, but it does not characterize global-\(L^2\) public-function minimax risk or an honest-length converse frontier. None of the opened papers characterizes minimax absolute risk, root mean-squared risk, fixed-probability error, and honest interval length for the same full-population ATE under bounded global prediction-error certificates, a fixed conditional-effect signal envelope, an explicit public-information decision class, and uniform one-sided shells.
fill: The core supplies an explicit public-information decision class, bounded nuisance radii, a fixed treatment-effect signal moment envelope, a single clipped estimator, a median amplification, four in-class converse channels whose regression amplitudes satisfy that envelope, the polynomial deterioration threshold, and an oracle bias-aware interval, all indexed by \(\rho_n\).
